title: Python Decorators: Write a Timer and a Cache
audience: Developers with a few months of Python experience who have seen the @ syntax but never written a decorator.
brief: Practical tutorial. The opening promises viewers will write a timing decorator and a caching decorator. Goal: viewers star the example repo linked in the description.

issues.description: The first 15 seconds are vague filler ('a thing in Python... a feature') that never says what decorators do or why the viewer should care.
Says decorators arrived in Python 3.9 in 2020. They were introduced in Python 2.4 in 2004 (PEP 318).
A roughly 40-second rant about tabs versus spaces, Neovim and a mechanical keyboard that is unrelated to decorators.
Spends over 30 seconds re-explaining what a function is, in repeated phrasing, to an audience that already writes Python.
The opening promises a caching decorator, but only the timing decorator is built; the video ends after asserting 'caching builds on the same idea'.
